gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the contribution claim that the compact-open UAT requires AP only on X as false or unsupported because the theorem and proof require AP on Y as well, specifically through approximation by finite-rank operators on Y.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The prose understates the hypotheses of the compact-open universal approximation theorem by omitting the required Approximation Property of Y, while the formal theorem and proof use AP for both X and Y.

component_coverage.gold_component: The compact-open UAT is incorrectly advertised as requiring AP on X alone, although the theorem setup and proof require AP on both X and Y.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies the AP-on-X-only claim, explains that the theorem assumes AP on both spaces, identifies the essential AP-on-Y proof step, and supplies the corresponding correction.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns the omitted Approximation Property hypothesis on the output space Y in a compact-open UAT. It contains no diagnosis of the separate rank-one claim for derivatives, nor of the zero-derivative counterexamples showing that only rank at most one is unconditional.
